candidates: When a PR modifies a regex that controls which characters are accepted as diagram syntax modifiers (e.g., the classifier/modifier regex in `classTypes.ts`), verify the accepted character set against the official mermaid documentation and explicitly assess whether removing previously-accepted characters—even undocumented ones—constitutes a safe breaking change for authors of existing diagrams.

When reviewing changes to a regex that captures modifier or classifier characters and feeds them into downstream logic (e.g., a switch or conditional block in `classTypes.ts`), verify that every character the updated regex can match is actually handled downstream. Characters accepted by the regex but absent from the downstream handler silently do nothing; their presence in older code often signals an accidental addition, and confirming this is the key evidence that their removal is safe.
